sections.title: Unit 1: What Are They Thinking? (동물 인지 과학)

sentences.zh: [Paragraph A (도입: 도구 사용과 문제 해결)] Animals demonstrate problem-solving abilities that challenge the idea that only humans possess advanced intelligence.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 까마귀(New Caledonian crows)가 철사를 구부려 도구를 만들고 병 속에 든 먹이를 꺼내는 실험. 이는 단순 시행착오가 아니라 사전 계획(planning)과 인과 추론에 기반함.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph B (자아 인식과 거울 실험)] Self-recognition in mirrors indicates a higher level of consciousness in certain animals.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 침팬지, 돌고래, 코끼리가 거울에 비친 자신의 몸에 묻은 점을 확인하고 닦아내는 행동. 이는 '나(Self)'라는 개념을 인식함을 증명.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph C (동물의 슬픔과 애도 - Grief)] Animals show emotional responses, particularly grief, when family members or companions die.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 코끼리 무리가 죽은 동료의 뼈 주위에 모여 오랜 시간 코로 만지며 침묵을 지키는 의식적 애도 행동.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph D (공감 능력 - Empathy in Rats & Dogs)] Recent scientific experiments reveal that empathy is not unique to humans.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 쥐 실험(Lever-pulling experiment) — 레버를 당기면 먹이가 나오지만 다른 쥐에게 전기 충격이 가해진다는 사실을 인지하자 쥐들이 레버 누르기를 중단함 (suffering 방지 본능).

sentences.zh: [Paragraph E (학계의 회의론과 반론 - Anthropomorphism)] Skeptics warn against anthropomorphism (인간화: 동물의 행동에 인간의 감정을 투영하는 오류).
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 동물의 특정 행동이 실제 감정인지, 단순한 조건반사적 생존 기제인지 엄밀한 과학적 검증이 필요하다는 주장.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph F & G (결론 및 시사점)] Expanding recognition of animal cognition reshapes how humans treat and protect nonhuman species.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 동물의 지능과 감정을 인정함으로써 동물 복지 법안, 사육 환경 개선, 생태계 보존의 도덕적 정당성이 확보됨.

sections.title: Unit 3: Living on an Urban Planet (메가시티와 도시화)

sentences.zh: [Paragraph A (도시 행성으로의 전환)] Humanity has crossed a historic threshold, transitioning into an predominantly urban species.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 과거 농경 중심 사회에서 산업화 이후 급격한 도시 집중. 1950년 인구 1,000만 이상의 메가시티는 뉴욕과 도쿄 2곳에 불과했으나 현재는 30개 이상으로 급증.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph B (도시 집중의 경제적 동인 - Push & Pull Factors)] Economic opportunities act as the strongest magnet drawing rural populations into cities.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 도시의 높은 소득 수준(income), 다양한 일자리, 교육 및 의료 인프라. 반면 농촌 지역의 일자리 부족과 기후 변화로 인한 농업 생산성 저하.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph C (도시의 생산성과 규모의 경제 - Productivity)] Dense concentrations of people foster greater economic productivity and technological innovation.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 지식 교류의 가속화, 인프라 공유로 인한 1인당 생산성 향상. 세계 GDP의 80% 이상이 도시에서 창출됨.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph D (도시 스프롤 현상과 교외화 - Sprawl & Suburbs)] Rapid population growth forces cities to spread out into surrounding rural areas, creating extensive suburbs.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 도심 지가 상승으로 인해 외곽으로의 확산(sprawl). 긴 통근 시간, 교통 체증, 탄소 배출 증가라는 부작용 야기.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph E (도시의 환경적 도전과 슬럼 문제)] Uncontrolled urban growth leads to severe infrastructural strain and social inequality.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 개발도상국 도시의 슬럼(무허가 빈민가) 형성, 식수 부족, 폐기물 처리 불능, 대기 및 수질 오염 심화.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph F & G (미래 도시 솔루션 - Green & Smart Cities)] Sustainable urban planning and technological innovations are essential to ensure the livability of future cities.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 대중교통 중심 개발(TOD), 녹지 공간 확충, 에너지 효율적 친환경 건축, 스마트 그리드 도입.

sections.title: Unit 5: The New Face of Tourism (지속 가능한 지오투어리즘)

sentences.zh: [Paragraph A (대중 관광의 폭발적 성장과 명암)] Global tourism has grown exponentially, bringing substantial economic gains but severe environmental strains.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 저비용 항공사(LCC)의 보급과 크루즈 여행 확대로 전 세계 해외 여행객 수가 14억 명을 돌파함.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph B (과잉 관광의 피해 사례 - Venice & Machu Picchu)] Fragile historic destinations are suffering irreversible damage due to mass visitor overcrowding.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 베네치아의 대형 크루즈선 파도로 인한 석조 기초 침식 및 현지 주민 유출; 마추픽추와 마야 유적의 계단 마모 및 폐기물 범람.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph C (새로운 관광 패러다임의 태동 - Geotourism)] Geotourism emerges as an alternative that sustains or enhances the geographical character of a place.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 내셔널 지오그래픽이 제안한 개념: 환경(environment), 문화(culture), 미학(aesthetics), 유산(heritage), 현지 주민의 복지(well-being)를 모두 보존하는 총체적 접근.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph D (지역 사회와의 상생 파트너십 - Partnerships)] Successful sustainable tourism depends on deep partnerships between tour operators and local residents.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 현지 주민을 공식 가이드(official guides)로 고용하여 정당한 생계(earn a living)를 보장하고, 수익이 다국적 기업이 아닌 지역 공동체로 환원되도록 구조화.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph E (재생 에너지와 친환경 숙박 시설 - Eco-friendly Hospitality)] Modern eco-lodges demonstrate that guest comfort can coexist with renewable and sustainable practices.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 태양광 및 지열 에너지 사용, 빗물 재활용, 일회용 플라스틱 퇴출, 현지 유기농 식자재 사용.

sentences.zh: [Paragraph F (여행자의 책임과 의식 고취 - Traveler Awareness)] Educating travelers to respect local culture and environment is vital for the long-term future of tourism.
sentences.kr: 핵심 세부 내용: 관광객 스스로가 탄소 발자국을 줄이고, 현지 규칙을 준수하며, 문화적 민감성을 발휘해야 한다는 인식 제고.

vocab.def_en: the way someone or something acts
vocab.ex: Even rats show human-like behavior in lab experiments.

vocab.def_en: a feeling of connection with someone or something else
vocab.ex: People often form strong bonds with animals they interact with.

vocab.def_en: relating to thinking and understanding
vocab.ex: Regular exercise can help with physical fitness and cognitive function.

vocab.def_en: involving a lot of different parts; difficult to understand
vocab.ex: Some believe emotions like sadness are too complex for nonhuman species.

vocab.def_en: causing disagreement
vocab.ex: The idea that animals feel emotions is controversial and sparks intense debate.

vocab.def_en: to train someone to follow rules or codes of behavior
vocab.ex: One way to discipline children is to establish a quiet timeout.

vocab.def_en: to create or start something that will last a long time
vocab.ex: Children generally sleep better when parents establish a regular bedtime routine.

vocab.def_en: a group that includes uncles, cousins, grandparents, etc.
vocab.ex: Previously, it was common for extended families to live together in one home.

vocab.def_en: the characteristics of being male or female
vocab.ex: It is normal for children, regardless of gender, to fear separation.

vocab.def_en: usually
vocab.ex: Researchers observed that children generally respond well to consistent schedules.

vocab.def_en: a very sad feeling (especially after someone dies)
vocab.ex: Some animals appear to express grief when a family member dies.

vocab.def_en: very great or extreme
vocab.ex: Children can experience an intense feeling of fear when lost.

vocab.def_en: to notice something after looking closely
vocab.ex: Biologists observed wolves cooperating in complex social groups.

vocab.def_en: before the time period that you are talking about
vocab.ex: Extended family households were far more common previously.

vocab.def_en: an understanding that something is true
vocab.ex: There is a growing recognition that animal minds are sophisticated.

vocab.def_en: occurring many times
vocab.ex: After doing this repeatedly, the animals mastered the maze.

vocab.def_en: to have something new or different instead of the original
vocab.ex: When birds shed feathers, new plumage grows to replace that which was lost.

vocab.def_en: the way a group of people or animals is organized
vocab.ex: Elephants maintain a matriarchal social structure led by the oldest female.

vocab.def_en: pain, either mental or physical
vocab.ex: The rats stopped pressing the lever to prevent the other rats suffering.

vocab.def_en: to behave toward someone or something in a particular way
vocab.ex: Society has a moral duty to treat living creatures with compassion.

vocab.def_en: a part or side of something
vocab.ex: One negative aspect of city living is chronic traffic congestion.

vocab.def_en: something that blocks movement or separates things
vocab.ex: Coastal cities construct storm surge barriers to block ocean surges.

vocab.def_en: an artificial waterway for boats or water conveyance
vocab.ex: Venice is internationally famous for its historic canals.

vocab.def_en: a huge amount or number of something in one place
vocab.ex: Metropolitan areas feature a dense concentration of economic talent.

vocab.def_en: the work or industry of building structures
vocab.ex: Hundreds of architects and engineers work in the construction industry.

vocab.def_en: having a large amount of something close together
vocab.ex: Some megacities are extremely dense, housing thousands per square kilometer.

vocab.def_en: powerful, violent, and aggressive (weather/storm)
vocab.ex: Low-lying cities suffer severe damage when struck by a fierce typhoon.

vocab.def_en: the process of increasing
vocab.ex: Rapid population growth forces municipal borders outward.

vocab.def_en: money that a person earns
vocab.ex: Urban workers generally earn higher average incomes than agricultural labor.

vocab.def_en: to move down or reduce the level/amount
vocab.ex: Hydraulic gates can lower or raise water levels during floods.

vocab.def_en: happening from time to time, not regularly
vocab.ex: What was once an occasional storm has now become an annual crisis.

vocab.def_en: partly, not completely
vocab.ex: During high tide, ground floors in Venice are partially submerged.

vocab.def_en: able to achieve a significant amount or result
vocab.ex: Knowledge-sharing clusters make urban professionals far more productive.

vocab.def_en: a person who lives in a particular place or area
vocab.ex: Every resident must be prepared for extreme weather occurrences.

vocab.def_en: to keep apart or divide
vocab.ex: Massive seawalls separate the rising ocean from inland residential zones.

vocab.def_en: to cover a huge area
vocab.ex: Metropolises continue to spread out into surrounding rural provinces.

vocab.def_en: areas outside of a large city that have homes and businesses
vocab.ex: Families often migrate to quiet suburbs seeking affordable single homes.

vocab.def_en: for a limited period of time; not permanently
vocab.ex: Stores had to close temporarily while municipal pumps drained floodwater.

vocab.def_en: to usually do something or be a certain way
vocab.ex: Cities tend to offer superior healthcare and university facilities.

vocab.def_en: relating to a city
vocab.ex: The planet has crossed the threshold into an urban majority.

vocab.def_en: one option instead of another
vocab.ex: Geotourism offers a sustainable alternative to destructive mass tourism.

vocab.def_en: knowledge that something exists
vocab.ex: The campaign aims to raise environmental awareness among international travelers.

vocab.def_en: a state of ease or well-being
vocab.ex: Modern eco-lodges provide luxury and comfort without depleting energy.

vocab.def_en: special; very different
vocab.ex: Venice possesses a distinctive architecture shaped by its marine canals.

vocab.def_en: to get money to pay for things that you need
vocab.ex: Indigenous residents earn a living as official eco-tour guides.

vocab.def_en: relating to the relationship between living things and their surroundings
vocab.ex: Resorts must calculate their ecological footprint prior to development.

vocab.def_en: the system by which a governments industry and money are organized
vocab.ex: The local island economy relies almost exclusively on overseas visitors.

vocab.def_en: providing more appreciation or enjoyment
vocab.ex: Authentic cultural exchanges make travel far more enriching than sightseeing.

vocab.def_en: damaging; dangerous
vocab.ex: Mass cruise exhaust produces harmful emissions that damage historic masonry.

vocab.def_en: a building or structure with historical or cultural significance
vocab.ex: Chichen Itza is a sacred Mayan landmark that draws millions annually.

vocab.def_en: to keep at a certain level
vocab.ex: Park authorities restrict tourist volume to maintain fragile trails.

vocab.def_en: essential; required
vocab.ex: Strict quotas are necessary to protect ancient ruins from overtourism.

vocab.def_en: a goal
vocab.ex: A primary objective of geotourism is the preservation of geographic character.

vocab.def_en: relating to a government or an organization
vocab.ex: All visitors must be escorted by official licensed indigenous guides.

vocab.def_en: a way of working with another person, group, or organization
vocab.ex: Sustainable travel requires an equal partnership between operators and locals.

vocab.def_en: to keep in a certain condition
vocab.ex: Nations establish marine sanctuaries to preserve endangered coral reefs.

vocab.def_en: able to be replaced naturally
vocab.ex: Eco-hotels generate electricity using renewable solar panels and wind turbines.

vocab.def_en: relating to a higher purpose rather than just material needs
vocab.ex: Indigenous communities attribute deep spiritual meaning to volcanic peaks.

vocab.def_en: able to continue in the long-term
vocab.ex: Sustainable tourism ensures heritage survives for future generations.

vocab.def_en: necessary or extremely important
vocab.ex: Educating international guests on cultural etiquette is of vital importance.

qa.question: [Q10] A state of ease or well-being.
options: economy      ### [Part 2] Contextual Cloze & Collocations (Questions 11 ~ 15) > **Directions**: Choose the best word or phrase to fill in the blank in each sentence.
qa.explanation: 어휘 영영 정의: comfort: a state of ease or well-being

qa.question: [Q11] After being hit by three major storms in a month, the historic seaside village had to close its harbor ______ while engineers completed structural repairs.
qa.explanation: 문맥 어휘 빈칸: temporarily: 수리 기간 동안 '일시적으로' 폐쇄

qa.question: [Q12] The mayor emphasized that raising public ______ regarding recycling practices is a vital prerequisite for building a green city.
qa.explanation: 문맥 어휘 콜로케이션: raise public awareness: 대중 인식을 고취하다

qa.question: [Q13] When wild animals feel threatened, they often display unpredictable ______ that can put observers in danger.
qa.explanation: 문맥 어휘 빈칸: unpredictable behavior: 예측 불가능한 행동 양식

qa.question: [Q14] Developing nations often struggle with uncontrolled urban sprawl because major cities continue to ______ into nearby agricultural zones.
qa.explanation: 문맥 어휘 구동사: spread out: 도시 외곽으로 뻗어나가다/확산되다

qa.question: [Q15] In order to ______ the ancient temple from acid rain and tourist vandalism, the government installed protective glass barriers.
options: lower      ### [Part 3] Reading Comprehension & Skill Analysis (Questions 16 ~ 23) > **Directions**: Read each passage and answer the questions based on the text.  #### [Passage 1: Animal Cognition] In a famous laboratory experiment, researchers presented New Caledonian crows with a container of meat floating in water that was too deep for their beaks to reach. Nearby, several wire hooks and straight pieces of wire were scattered on the table. Without prior training, one crow named Betty selected a straight piece of wire, bent one end against a crevice in the cage to fashion a curved hook, and successfully lifted the meat basket out of the container. This extraordinary feat demonstrated that the crow was not merely relying on trial and error, but was capable of understanding physical cause-and-effect relationships and formulating a multi-step plan in advance.
qa.explanation: 문맥 어휘 빈칸: preserve: 산성비와 훼손으로부터 사원을 '보존하다'

qa.question: [Q16] What is the main idea of Passage 1?
options: New Caledonian crows have the largest brain-to-body ratio among all bird species.
Betty the crow proved that animals can invent tools through cognitive planning rather than simple chance.
Laboratory experiments on animals frequently produce controversial and untrustworthy results.
Using wire hooks is an innate survival skill passed down through crow generations.
qa.explanation: 독해 대의 파악: 인지적 계획을 통한 도구 제작 증명 (Main Idea)

qa.question: [Q17] Which detail from the passage directly supports the claim that the crow understood physical cause-and-effect?
options: The meat was floating in deep water.
Several straight wires were scattered on the table.
The crow bent the straight wire against a crevice to fashion a hook before trying to retrieve the food.

The container was placed inside a laboratory cage.      #### [Passage 2: Urban Living] Today, over half of humanity lives in urban areas, and by 2050, that figure is projected to exceed two-thirds. Cities occupy just three percent of the planet's land surface, yet they generate over 80 percent of global gross domestic product. This intense concentration of economic activity and human capital creates tremendous advantages: knowledge spreads rapidly between innovative companies, and infrastructure like water and mass transit can be delivered more cost-effectively per person than in dispersed rural towns. However, rapid urbanization is not without severe drawbacks. When municipal governments fail to build affordable housing and manage growth, sprawling informal settlements known as slums expand rapidly, lacking basic sanitation and clean drinking water.
qa.explanation: 세부 근거(Supporting): 구부려서 갈고리를 먼저 만드는 계획적 행동

qa.question: [Q18] According to Passage 2, what is one major reason why cities produce so much wealth?
options: Rural residents donate a significant portion of their income to metropolitan projects.
The dense concentration of people enables rapid knowledge sharing and cost-effective infrastructure.
Cities occupy over 80 percent of the Earth's total land area.
Governments ban commercial activity outside metropolitan boundaries.
qa.explanation: 세부 팩트 확인: 인구 집중으로 인한 지식 공유 및 인프라 효율성

qa.question: [Q19] What causes the expansion of sprawling informal settlements (slums)?
options: Too much investment in mass transit systems.
A decline in global gross domestic product.
The failure of municipal governments to manage growth and provide affordable housing.

Excessive dispersal of people into remote rural towns.      #### [Passage 3: Sustainable Tourism] The tiny island nation of Palau in the western Pacific was once overwhelmed by tourists who damaged coral reefs, discarded plastic waste, and disturbed marine ecosystems. Recognizing that traditional mass tourism was eroding the very natural assets that attracted visitors, the government adopted a groundbreaking approach called the "Palau Pledge." Upon arrival, every foreign traveler must stamp their passport with a legal commitment to act in an environmentally responsible manner. Furthermore, single-use plastics and reef-toxic sunscreens were completely outlawed, and visitors pay a mandatory green fee that directly funds conservation partnerships with indigenous marine rangers.
qa.explanation: 인과 추론: 주택 공급 및 도시 관리 실패로 인한 슬럼화

qa.question: [Q20] What problem initially prompted the government of Palau to change its tourism policy?
options: The economy collapsed because tourists refused to visit the island.
Foreign tour operators refused to employ indigenous islanders.
Mass tourism was severely damaging the island's coral reefs and marine ecosystem.
Hotel companies were unable to find renewable sources of solar energy.
qa.explanation: 세부 팩트 확인: 대중 관광으로 인한 산호초 및 해양 생태계 파괴

qa.question: [Q21] How does the Palau government fund its conservation partnerships with indigenous rangers?
options: By borrowing money from multinational banking organizations.
By collecting a mandatory green fee from foreign visitors.
By selling historic landmarks to international hotel chains.
By permitting cruise ships to anchor directly on coral reefs.
qa.explanation: 세부 팩트 확인: 외국인 대상 의무적 green fee 징수를 통한 기금 조성

qa.question: [Q22] Which of the following words best describes the Palau Pledge?
options: An optional questionnaire about traveler preferences.
A commercial contract that allows tourists to collect marine specimens.
A legal commitment signed by incoming visitors to protect the environment.
A temporary guideline that applies only during stormy seasons.
